note: SEALED fresh holdout built 2026-10-28 AFTER the fault_type taxonomy was frozen and after v2 was disclosed as post-hoc. New fictional company, new values, new hiding places for two faults. Never shown to the model, never used for tuning, expected_findings.json is never included in the model prompt. First run on this set is a first-sight measurement.
pass_bar: Model catches >=4 of 5 faults on data it has never seen, in the Oct 31 credibility runs. Report strict + typed scores side by side, same as v2.

findings.description: The purchase events report currency 'GBP' with value 144.00, but the whole funnel ran in USD — every earlier event uses currency USD and the items were priced at USD 48.00 x 3. Revenue for this order is recorded in the wrong currency.
findings.expected_fix: Send the currency the customer actually paid in (USD) on the purchase event; add a schema check that event currency matches item prices/storefront currency.

findings.description: The identical purchase event — same transaction_id HP-2026-7319, same items, same value — is recorded twice, 4 seconds apart. A double-fired tag records one order as two purchases and doubles reported revenue.
findings.expected_fix: De-duplicate on transaction_id at the tag/trigger level and in the reporting pipeline.

findings.description: A live shipping-rates API key is hidden inside the Shipping Rates custom HTML tag: a base64 blob decoded with atob() at runtime holds {hp_rates_key: HP_TOKEN_f4k3...}. Encoding is not protection — anyone who can view the container can decode it, and the key ships to every visitor's browser.
findings.expected_fix: Revoke/rotate the key, move the rates lookup server-side, and never ship credentials — encoded or not — in a client-side tag.

findings.description: payments.charge_card ran with idempotency_key null. When the first attempt timed out at the gateway, the client retried and the customer was charged twice: two settled charges (ch_hp_441, ch_hp_442) of 14400 cents each for one order — a real double charge.
findings.expected_fix: Require a stable idempotency key (the order reference) on every charge call so gateway retries collapse into one charge; refund the duplicate charge.

findings.description: A customer's email address and phone number sit in the INPUT of the notifications.send_receipt call, so they are stored in the trace log in plain text. Inputs get logged just like outputs — this trace now holds personal contact data.
findings.expected_fix: Pass an order/customer reference instead of raw email/phone, and redact PII from tool inputs before the trace is persisted.
